seoTitle: How to Contact Stripe Support by Email or Live Chat
metaDescription: Reach Stripe support through your dashboard's Support center or the public Support site, use the Assistant to pick a topic, then chat or email.
intro: Stripe gives you two real doors into support: the Support center built into your Dashboard, and the public Stripe Support site that opens an Assistant chat before connecting you to a human agent or email. Which one you use matters less than picking the right topic and giving support enough detail to actually act on, since a vague "payments aren't working" message gets a slower response than one naming the specific issue. This guide walks through both entry points and the Assistant flow that decides whether you end up in live chat or an email thread.

steps.heading: Open the Support center in your Dashboard
steps.body: From inside your Stripe Dashboard, the left sidebar's Support center lists Support cases, File requests, Shared files, and Support team as tabs, with filters for All, Open, and Closed cases. A fresh account shows "No support conversations found" here, which is expected — this is the tracking view for cases you've already opened, not where you start a new one, but it's worth knowing this exists so you can find a case again later instead of hunting through email.

image.caption: The Support center inside the Stripe Dashboard, listing Support cases, File requests, Shared files, and Support team tabs.

steps.heading: Start a new request from the Stripe Support site
steps.body: To actually open a new request, go to Stripe's public Support site rather than the in-Dashboard tracker. It leads with a "How can we help?" search box and a list of popular articles — trouble signing in, waiting on your first payout, adding a bank account — which is worth a quick scan first, since Stripe notes some of these solve the large majority of the users who read them.

steps.heading: Use the Assistant to select your topic
steps.body: If the articles don't cover your issue, the Assistant panel on the same page asks you to select the account your question applies to, then pick a topic from a scrollable list — Disputes, Financial Reports, Stripe Issuing, Login Issues, Data Migrations, Payment APIs, and more. Choosing the right topic here matters because it's what routes your question correctly; picking a topic close to your actual issue rather than a generic catch-all gets you to a useful answer faster.

image.caption: The Assistant panel on Stripe's Support site, asking which account and topic your question applies to before routing you further.

steps.heading: Choose live chat or email based on urgency
steps.body: Once you've described the problem to the Assistant, it offers a path to a support agent — either a live conversation or, if you'd rather not wait, an email option like "Send us an email" with a clear note that an agent will respond within 24 hours. A text box lets you describe the issue in your own words — something specific like "my payouts are not working properly" — before you attach any files and hit Send.

image.caption: The Assistant's email option, with a 24-hour response note and a text box for describing the issue before sending.

steps.heading: Write a description that gets a faster answer
steps.body: Whether you end up in chat or email, the difference between a fast resolution and a slow back-and-forth is usually how specific your first message is. Include the account it affects, the type of issue (a specific payout, a disputed charge, a failed API call), and any error text you saw verbatim rather than paraphrased — support agents can look up exact error messages and transaction IDs far faster than they can decode "it's broken."

steps.heading: Track the conversation afterward
steps.body: Once your request is submitted, whether by chat or email, it shows up back in the Dashboard's Support center under Support cases, moving from Open to Closed once it's resolved. Checking there is the fastest way to follow up on a case without digging through your email inbox, and it's also where you'd go to reopen a case if the same issue comes back.

faq.question: Is Stripe support available 24/7?
faq.answer: The Assistant and Support site are accessible any time, but live agent availability and email response windows (Stripe notes around 24 hours for email) can vary by account type and region.

faq.question: Do I need a paid Stripe plan to get support?
faq.answer: No — every Stripe account has access to the Support center and the public Support site's Assistant, article search, chat, and email options, regardless of plan.

faq.question: How fast does Stripe respond to email support?
faq.answer: The Assistant's email option sets expectations upfront, generally around 24 hours for a first response, so live chat is the better choice for anything urgent like a payment outage.

faq.question: What information should I have ready before contacting support?
faq.answer: Have the affected account, a specific description of the issue, any exact error text, and relevant IDs (payout, charge, or dispute) ready — the more specific your first message, the faster the Assistant or an agent can route and resolve it.

faq.question: Where do I find a support case I already opened?
faq.answer: Open the Support center from your Stripe Dashboard sidebar and check the Support cases tab, filtering by Open or Closed to find the specific conversation.
